text: The 10/1 m11 point extends the same anchored curve toward the measured 20/1 tail in a38fee52661fd3e3b7ea before the 50/1 result 9ffee2813aef5c26f96f, improving tail-shape learning.
Tests m22 at 20/1 and 150 uL in a high predicted interval regime, adding a chemically distinct condition-response anchor.
Adds a lower-condition, lower-amount m125 setup point to distinguish baseline loading behavior from the observed high-retention branch.

Molecule-novel oxygen-rich scaffold with extreme predicted widths (V1 72.9, V2 43.3) and maximum CW distance. It tests transfer of late-tail behavior seen in m107 and m216 failures such as c6924324ddd95f249df6 and e47aebe2660b9e1528de.

m95 at 10/1, 150 uL extends the loading series containing measured 10/1, 50-uL record 41f57dc6d50ee162801. It tests whether the observed onset decrease with loading continues at the larger loading amount and whether V2 follows it.

m122 at 20/1, 150 uL extends a substituted aromatic ether/benzophenone-like family into a high-PE condition. It tests endpoint allocation where aromaticity and oxygen count alone are insufficient structural descriptors.

m159 was 4.91/18.96 mL at 5/1 in 6aa69f7c2b8244353a75 and about 57.9/117.9 mL at 50/1 in a17bcdddcf0799baeee2 and 1395836aef00d6a880b. This 10/1 point maps the rapid response before the extreme ratio.
The observed molecule-novel m200 point at 1/1 in 97318de99bab4460cf4 was underpredicted at 15.15/37.4 mL. This 2/1 measurement tests whether the underprediction continues with stronger mobile phase.

The 1/1 m200 point changes loading relative to the measured 1/1 row 97318de99bab4460cf4 and complements the measured 2/1 high-loading point a92f7617b135de150588. It tests transfer and loading sensitivity in a novel polar aromatic scaffold.

A weak-condition m203 anchor gives a baseline for the late measured row 9ed7c1fb1c2cc499bbf and the higher-ratio candidate in this batch. It helps identify whether the model's V2 error is a regime transition or a molecule-wide offset.

m177 repeatedly has nonzero measured onset while the model predicts a floor onset at nearby 10/1 and 20/1 conditions, including aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 and 5442611ea6789d42bc86. This 5/1 point localizes where the onset-floor failure begins.
The m177 20/1, 150 ul point tests whether the short-tail behavior at 20/1 and 50 ul in aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 persists at higher loading, where a genuine loading-dependent V2 expansion is plausible.
This m177 50/1, 50 ul point is a critical loading anchor against 4862e2fb71344ce16021 and b514312eda7950cdcf1c, whose measured V2 values differ sharply with loading.
This m72 2/1, low-volume DCM point bridges the measured 1/1-to-5/1 response and tests whether the broad V2 behavior seen at 5/1 and 20/1 emerges gradually.
m153 at 0/1 DCM and 150 ul provides a strong-solvent halogenated aromatic baseline for calibrating the lower-volume boundary of non-donor molecules.
m72 at 10/1 DCM and 150 ul fills a high-ratio response point near the late heteroatom-rich regimes measured in 855832bd4005ac7abdc and 49201b5817f204116f7f.
m90 at 0/1 DCM establishes an early baseline before the strong ratio-dependent behavior represented by measured 855832bd4005ac7abdc.
m90 at 5/1 DCM with 50 ul tests whether the late m90 regime persists at lower loading, complementing measured high-error m90 behavior in 855832bd4005ac7abdc and 49201b5817f204116f7f.
m125 at 2/1 DCM tests the transition toward the measured m125 high-ratio tail while remaining a useful local interpolation point.
m63 at 20/1 and 100 ul provides a substituted fused-ketone comparator under matched nominal conditions, testing graph-specific effects on response slope.

Complete a fixed-loading m65 ratio pair at 50/1, predicted at 10.15/23.31 with CW distance approximately 0.890. Two labels on this new graph can distinguish a genuinely shallow ketone response from extrapolation error and provide more transferable supervision than two nearly identical loading rows.

Introduce molecule-novel bromopropylbenzene m1 at 50/1 and 100 ul. Its chloro analogue is measured under closely comparable PE loading conditions in ff36ed72f76515960408. The predicted bromide endpoints, 8.04/11.42, test whether halogen substitution transfers correctly while accounting for the associated density-times-volume amount change.

m27 at 1/1 supplies a lower-strength baseline for the measured m27 sequence. The observed m27 rows 8748c66e5f0823e6a65, c0adb1c6f9dbe862a4dc and a3c1a0ac40733e8650fb show an unexpectedly shallow and short response, so this label tests the lower boundary without assuming renewed growth.

The model predicts a broad late interval for a heteroatom-rich row at 10/1 DCM and high loading. It extends the underpredicted late regime seen for m107 and m118 in c6924324ddd95f249df6 and 2d178efe0181baca2bd5.

This high-width 50/1 DCM row tests whether a carbonyl-rich scaffold enters a late regime at larger sample volume. The m177 loading contrast in b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 4862e2fb71344ce16021 shows that apparently similar strong-condition rows can have very different tails.

A high-width 10/1 DCM point for an oxygen-rich ester scaffold probes the onset-to-finish transition between ordinary and extreme carbonyl retention, informed by the measured m107 and m118 failures in c6924324ddd95f249df6 and 2d178efe0181baca2bd5.

This high-width 10/1 DCM aldehyde/ester-like row tests a strong-condition upper tail in a scaffold distinct from the measured m195 and m198 examples. It is useful for distinguishing family-specific high-ratio behavior from a global correction.

m189 at 10/1, 100 uL is predicted at 5.33/20.18 mL. Same-loading 5/1 record 5edaf16084f46f5b4726 and recent 20/1 record fd9cda2d3ab32ea2a360 measured 5.63/14.57 and 4.39/23.10 mL. This tests finish growth with little onset delay in a biphenyl aldehyde, a pattern the model previously coupled too strongly.

Novel amino-nitrile-like m160 scaffold at 5/1 DCM and 100 ul, with predicted V1/V2 20.75/53.97 ml and a 13.91-ml V1 width. It expands coverage of donor/acceptor-rich aromatic chemistry beyond the heavily represented families.
m195 at 50/1 targets finish calibration after the anomalous measured interval at a917c928912c74862968a; it can distinguish true broadening from model interval pathology.
m120 5/1, 50-ul point completes the loading curve between e4fd83fb3852eb354a66 at 100 ul and 20913a7c2077b80b7351 at 150 ul, where V2 changed disproportionately.
Low-load 5/1 m216 point completes the loading contrast to measured 5/1 150-ul c5185bd663026c64c816 and sits below the 10/1 tail records e47aebe2660b9e1528de and 9cd02352c2ed7a3e232.
Provides a 100-ul m28 loading anchor at fixed 1/1 DCM; the broad measured m28 tails at bfbe491a54086b98874d and 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40 make this useful for separating loading from solvent effects.

Matched 150-ul m28 point at the same nominal solvent condition tests whether loading expands V2 independently of onset, building on the large m28 finish errors in bfbe491a54086b98874d and 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40.
High-CW m141 tests a heteroaromatic, low-density regime against the severe measured m141 response in 7fb4f90753d40dd25be, helping repair local V1/V2 offsets.
The m25 2/1 point extends the compact carbonyl control beyond the measured 0/1 condition 0af4d354d29927a8a743 and checks whether V2 corrections remain centered as mobile-phase ratio changes.

The model predicts 4.85/10.95 ml for low-strength m159. This baseline is essential for separating the ordinary response from the extreme measured high-strength tail in a17bcdddcf0799baeee2 and the intermediate behavior in d3d2b36ec3417c1c1c6c.

m96 at 1/1 provides an additional compact sulfur-containing low-strength anchor, complementing the measured compact point 914cbf3bfe7468210e0 and broad higher-strength points such as 5bad82a6cffd60e7a6c9.

This m177 50/1 point reduces loading relative to the extreme observed tail b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 5e276c1730fc0a9deba. The matched scaffold contrast directly tests whether V2 tail size is loading-sensitive.
A low-strength, lower-loading m177 anchor tests whether the large finish widths in b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 5e276c1730fc0a9deba are activated by solvent strength, loading, or both.

This lower-strength m141 point tests where the severe heteroaromatic transition begins. It complements the observed 2/1 and 10/1 m141 regimes in 8436939a2a6a91fa470d, eceaa4f4139cde7ba166, and 7fb4f90753d40dd25be.
m107 at 2/1 with half the sample volume of the measured 60b7eed7a46a03b366b2 and f96cee9775323fbf1d8 rows isolates loading from the nonlinear strength response seen in 2cfa393cb79664e100ce.

This intermediate m178 condition sits between measured compact behavior at 0/1 in aed6d224edcb21e5d658 and late behavior at 10/1 and 50/1 in 634f21e11a8442494ce3 and 0c5c35afb3a24375c153, providing a boundary anchor.

This m17 10/1 point extends strength coverage for an ester-like scaffold and can test whether its predicted shift follows the local strength response seen in the measured m208 sequence 09b5473d1d8ee26da8d, 1150272392a90f36db05, 457b3def1714039eadb3, and b66aa101a244885dd587.
Measure m70, a long-chain aryl ketone, at 0/1 and 150 ul as a lipophilic control for compact retention and finish behavior.

The batch combines local response experiments and broad failure repair. The m177, m159, m91, m92, m124, m123, and m39 groups provide repeated molecules across solvent strength and loading, with several measured anchors such as 5e276c1730fc0a9deba, e2f15590b7142490599b, 1844eab177de5d01fab6, ba56f0e652a97bcee1b2, and 5524670e4337370c2ef6. This should teach condition-retention interactions and loading sensitivity. The other selections cover high-cw long-tail chemistry, extreme loading regimes, and direct quantile pathologies such as inverted or nearly zero-width intervals. Together they sample both common local relationships and rare V1/V2 regions that can disproportionately affect overall error, while maintaining scaffold and condition diversity for generalization across the Row-distribution.

For m177 the model predicts V1=0.0 mL with a 9.76 mL V1 quantile width and cw distance 0.97. This changes loading and solvent strength relative to measured 5e276c1730fc0a9deba and tests whether the low-V1 failure is real.

This is a direct loading contrast for m177 at 20/1: 50 uL here versus 150 uL in measured 5e276c1730fc0a9deba. The predicted V1/V2 of 4.59/56.95 mL can identify loading effects separately from the observed condition response.
A lower-volume m159 condition separates mobile-phase response from loading sensitivity in a scaffold with a broad predicted tail.

Bromobenzonitrile at 1/1 supplies a strong-eluent nitrile/halogen anchor and tests whether the model separates nitrile polarity from the late basic-nitrogen family represented by 49201b5817f204116f7f and 9cd02352c2ed7a3e232.

Long-chain acrylate at 5/1 tests hydrophobic chain-size effects in an ester graph and complements the measured long-chain response c2631e65cfde93b7bbd64 and condition-novel ether acrylate c11d5c3acbc28dddd0cf.
High-CW-distance donor-free fused aromatic at 20/1. It tests whether the model transfers the ordinary nonpolar response seen in m210 and m9 to a larger fused graph.
A halogenated aromatic ester at 50/1 samples a weak-eluent endpoint for a donor-free oxygenated graph and tests whether simple esters remain narrower than the measured m94 and m125 tails.
Difluorobenzaldehyde at 10/1 is a low-complexity carbonyl/halogen anchor. It can distinguish carbonyl response from the broad tails measured for m193 and m31.
Dimethoxytoluene at 2/1 supplies a simple ether-rich aromatic reference at moderate condition, helping distinguish ether effects from the measured m125 aldehyde response.
Tertiary cyclohexanol at 1/1 tests steric shielding of an alcohol donor and helps separate local alcohol environment from broad polarity, using measured m204 and m60 failures as context.
An aminobenzoate at 10/1 tests whether an aniline donor changes the ester response in the same general region as the large V2 residuals for m86 and m89.
A fluorinated fused diketone at 10/1 is a high-CW carbonyl anchor with broad predicted endpoints. It tests graph-conditioned V2 transfer from measured m26, m31, and m166 residual regions.
Amino ester at 10/1 and high loading extends the accessible aromatic-nitrogen region represented by measured 9a60eec5ad3051be568a and 84e60b516f17f5433041.
Amino acrylate at 10/1 provides an accessible nitrogen and ester anchor complementary to the measured amino-acrylate response in 9a60eec5ad3051be568a.
The low-loading 5/1 m13 point gives a matched contrast to measured 5/1 m13 row 5d530b2f228ed39ff952 and the very late 10/1 row 9e3e08d6bc42e91e2679.
Low loading m141 at 2/1 tests the ratio-response branch between observed 835b5f2641442576de42 and eceaa4f4139cde7ba166, after the late m141 tails in 51f4126a3aadb323922 and 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0.
Low-loading 10/1 m216 tests whether the measured 10/1 tails in 9cd02352c2ed7a3e232 and 222a68fc192f66c1c080 persist when amount is reduced.
The weak-ratio m161 loading point contrasts with 0c24b9414856413c9a67, f9d4d16c9703edbbe541f, and 247846e36e9c012df30f to identify the low-end baseline before the large 5/1 tail.
A high-ratio m95 point tests whether the extreme completion behavior in 5fd0921bbbba1e22abf is specific to loading; the lower-ratio anchor 41f57dc6d50ee162801a provides a condition comparison.
The 0/1, low-loading m216 anchor is a direct amount contrast to eb56f25c331ea1ab9b2b and tests whether the completion tail is already present at weak elution.

First label for tetralone m180 at 20/1 tests transfer from the closely related seven-membered ketone b8b8becd233748ccae9e3 and methyl-substituted fused ketone f9bba2e75f16ebadb0eb. High structural similarity makes this a focused test of ring-size encoding and condition transfer within a common carbonyl family.
m196 at 20/1 extends weak-eluent response for a brominated fused aldehyde and tests transfer from measured m196 rows f5477c41d918e49abba1 and 7c6e7b244de393e8554d.
m162 at higher loading complements the measured 1/1 row f779e666959ebae2ab4 and tests whether loading changes a nitrile-containing neutral anchor.

m140 provides a neutral iodotoluene control at 2/1. It helps prevent the model from transferring late basic or donor behavior to heavy-halogen aromatics, against measured m140 examples such as 8f84fa7c65453783c74e8.

m178 at 5/1 samples below the measured 20/1 and 50/1 records 855456da9ea892f7216b and 0c5c35afb3a24375c153. It tests whether the late rise begins gradually or remains suppressed until a higher solvent ratio.

m209 at 10/1 and 50 uL fills the solvent-response curve above measured 1/1 and 2/1 points f7e3bf988bd0e1b9f58b and eda42a3c0f94ffce3e99, while remaining below the strong PE behavior 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf. It tests the onset of its late transition.
Strong-eluent aniline ester at low loading, providing a matched loading contrast to the selected m88 high-loading point.

Intermediate-condition m146 measurement probes where the graph-specific late transition begins, between compact lower-ratio observations and severe 10/1 and 10/1 high-loading rows (9e3ce3497298084abd83, 23ef03f3e75e40b20095).

Measure lactone m181 at 1/1, 100 uL below its measured 5/1 response in 8fb92bd1fab3ba235858 and 10/1 response in 989b2145455d703d3b6d's neighboring measured curve anchors 2cc7c8ae52cdb25ca284 and 64c9e190e213bb061867. This tests the onset of the lactone-specific retention rise.
